title: Just keeps you on your phone
body:
This app claims to help you improve your habits but it is designed to have you spend as much time as possible on the app and not in the real world. Habits as simple as drinking water (which is the first one they force you to add even if you’re already doing it) take 5 minutes to check off. The app is overwhelming and designed to keep you on your phone rather than practicing healthy habits. The core concept is good and I’m sure the science behind the visualisation and making habits easier to stick to tracks but the app is full of unnecessary distractions. It clashes with the core mission advertised. 

Plus, the free trail led to having me sign up for £120 worth of monthly subscriptions. They are not linked to your apple account so you cannot easily cancel and each feature has to be cancelled individually. You then have to sign in again to cancel the next one. Even more proof this app doesnt care about you creating healthy habits and just wants to keep you on the app and paying huge subscriptions. Steer clear. Read up on the principles behind habit stacking and leave the app well alone.

title: Preys on people looking for help
body:
Misleading subscription design – particularly concerning for an app targeting ADHD and burnout

I downloaded Fabulous after being specifically targeted with advertising suggesting it could help with ADHD and burnout. Unfortunately, my experience of the app has been the opposite.

The set-up process feels deliberately designed to blur the line between simply progressing through onboarding and committing to additional paid subscriptions. I was repeatedly presented with what appeared to be “next steps”, only to find they were actually one-click subscription commitments to additional services/apps. For something specifically marketed towards people who may already struggle with overwhelm, attention and executive function, I find this particularly troubling.

Once subscribed, figuring out exactly what I had signed up for and how to cancel was a complicated maze. The sheer number of prompts, offers and additional subscription opportunities made the whole experience feel less like onboarding and more like a carefully designed sales funnel.

Having gone through all of that, what I seem to have ended up with is essentially a very expensive reminder to drink water.

I appreciate that subscription apps need to make money, but users should understand clearly when they are making a purchase, what they are purchasing and how much it will cost. In my experience, that clarity was completely lacking.

I would like the subscriptions I inadvertently signed up for through this process cancelled and the charges refunded. I would strongly encourage Fabulous to reconsider an onboarding and payment design that feels particularly inappropriate given the audience it is actively targeting.

title: More of a scam than help for people with ADHD
body:
Spoiler: hidden subscriptions and complicated cancellation process. £100 has been taken out of my account despite me believing I had unsubscribed.

Having been struggling with ADHD I fell for the slick instagram adverts and was excited to give Fabulous a go. I started a one week trial and then downloaded Clarity as well because this was pushed to me by the app as the one you actually need for ADHD. 

Firstly, the apps are so busy there’s way too much going on and the duo-lingo gamification meant I would have to work up to being able to just have a simple weekly routine checklist put together. So I cancelled - or so I thought - my subscriptions days before the free trial ended. 

Jump to now, where several payments from thefab.co have been taken out of my account totalling over £100. Apparently, during the process of signing up, ON THE APP, I had also made several additional subscriptions to all these other platforms via the website - the subscriptions do not show when you look on the App Store and are conveniently hidden on the website. 

I’m so angry and upset, that in trying to feel more on top of my life I’ve been totally taken advantage of. I will be trying to get a refund if anyone else has successfully done so let me know.

title: BEWARE: SLICK BILLING LEFT ME WITH 9 UNKNOWN CHARGES
body:
I downloaded this app believing I was starting a simple trial, but what followed was extremely confusing and expensive.

What I did not understand at the time was that signing up created three separate recurring subscriptions connected to an Apple “Hide My Email” relay address. The subscriptions did not appear in my visible Apple subscription settings, and after deleting the app I believed the billing issue had been resolved.

I received onboarding emails, but I did not receive clear billing or renewal notifications that alerted me recurring charges were continuing. Over time, close to £300 was taken from my account before I realised what had happened.

The company refunded only the most recent charges and refused reimbursement for earlier renewals despite repeated attempts to resolve the issue.

Before signing up, I would strongly advise users to:

* check whether multiple subscriptions are being activated,
* check whether “Hide My Email” is being used,
* verify where subscriptions are managed,
* and confirm exactly how cancellation works.

I have since found substantial online discussion from other users describing similar confusion around billing and subscription management.

title: Preying on vulnerable people
body:
After seeing ads for this app dozens of times every day presenting itself as the solution for people struggling with ADHD, designed by academics, I caved and said I’d try it for just under a pound. As a disabled and chronically ill person, I do not have a lot of money to spare on something that won’t even really tell me what it is and simply promises to change my life. Instead of learning more during the sign-up process, I mostly remember it just being a series of upsells for yet more vague apps and subscriptions.
I did my best to find how to decline the upsell again and again and when I finally got to try out the app, I quickly realised that it would not work for me. Before being able to do anything else, you need to make a solemn promise to yourself that includes remembering every day that you are going to die. I do not need that kind of anxiety trigger and it suggested a vibe of pressure to be productive to me that is not compatible with taking care of my mental health while chronically ill.
I ended up deleting the app and thought that was that until I see a month later that 35 pounds have been taken from my bank account. I was not aware of committing to a subscription that would 40x in price between month 1 and 2 and I did not receive any communication in advance of the renewal or debiting my account. In order to find how to cancel the subscription, I had to re-download the app and go through another five-minute tutorial before being able to navigate to my account settings.
As an app that advertises relentlessly to people with ADHD who are struggling, not sending any heads up and then making the process so convoluted reads as clearly predatory to me.

title: A gift to you from yourself
body:
Honestly;

I've been using the FABULOUS app for a few months now, and I cannot express how transformative it has been for my daily routine. The app combines science-backed techniques with a beautifully designed interface, making it easy to stay motivated.

**Pros:**

1. **User-Friendly Interface:** The layout is clean and intuitive, making navigation a breeze.

2. **Personalised Journey:** The app tailors its recommendations based on your goals, whether it’s improving productivity, building healthy habits, or enhancing well-being.

3. **Daily Reminders:** I love the gentle nudges that keep me on track without feeling overwhelming.

4. **Diverse Content:** From guided meditations to science-based articles, there’s a wealth of resources to explore.

5. **Community Support:** The ability to connect with others on similar journeys adds an element of accountability and encouragement.

**Cons:**

- The premium features are excellent, but I wish some more advanced options were available in the free version.

Overall, FABULOUS has helped me cultivate better habits and prioritise my mental health. I highly recommend it to anyone looking to enhance their life and embrace a more positive mindset!

body: This app is a scam. The company is unethical at best, fraudulent at worst. Even though I subscribed via apple pay it doesn’t show up in subscriptions as they handle billing outside the Apple/Google ecosystem, so you can’t cancel on your phone at all, nor in the app. Even on the website it’s not clear where the subscriptions are found and you have to find each subscription and cancel them individually. Read other reviews and Reddit threads for reports of users repeatedly being charged having cancelled, sometimes much later, and unknowingly having subscribed to large monthly payments (which the company then refuses to refund). Same copy and paste response to every negative comment but it’s clearly a big issue. Avoid at all costs. I ended up cancelling my card as a fail-safe, as I simply don’t trust this company. body:

How in the heck do you guys still have my financial details after I DELETED the account? Disgusting behaviour.

title: Predatory subscription model - no-monthly design
body: I downloaded Fabulous with the intention of improving my habits and managing my ADHD symptoms. However, the app’s subscription practices are misleading and disappointing. Fabulous uses a non-standard bi-monthly (every two months) billing cycle, which is not clearly disclosed during signup. For those with ADHD, financial management can already be a challenge, and Fabulous appears to exploit this by making it harder to monitor subscriptions. I attempted to cancel and contacted customer service, but the support provided was unhelpful. An app that claims to support people with ADHD should have transparent, ethical billing practices. This feels disingenuous and predatory. I would not recommend this app based on my experience.

title: Designed to exploit, do not trust
body:
I wish I'd read some of these other one star reviews before signing up for the subscription. I feel like an idiot for falling for it. I enjoyed the trial. I liked the application enough that I paid full price for the first month. I stopped using it, and I decided the cancel before the second month. I tried to cancel. I wasn't billed for several months - and I thought I'd cancelled it successfully, then I was hit with three bills that added up to £128.97 at once.

It feels deliberate. This was a targetted ad that I had on Instagram, and the ad specifically targetted people with ADHD. You can't just open the application and cancel it - when you open the application up, it will greet you with a quiz / features and until you navigate through before you can even get to your account settings. There's no way to close it or get at them quickly. You have to open the web page up in the browser, sign in again, and navigate through a form that is intentionally confusing / diverts your attention away with multiple screens presenting you with offers, asking why you've chosen to leave, etc. There's one in particular where you have to make a selection between to survey options to continue that is just not intuitive at all - and they all kind of look like, if you're not really paying attention, like they're confirming that you have cancelled / optional survey questions once you've completed the process. You haven't.

They say it is designed to try to hwlp structure your day but it really feels like it's designed to obfuscate as much about the app, and their other apps as possible. You can't easily flick around the features and decide which are the right ones for you. As I mentioned before, even getting to the app's main landing/home screen can take a bit of effort some days, if it decides it wants to quiz you first. While having an explore in my trial week I downloaded a couple of their other apps to try to have a look at them too - and without realising to or recalling how, I seem to have committed to their 'bundle' package, with an additional £46.99 bimonthly charge that I never wanted to sign up for and have just been billed for twice at once. I don't remember being asked about this at all, but it wasn't really that clear whether those apps were included in the £34.99  or not until I clicked within tje Fabulous app to download them. I didn't use them, free trial or else, but they've managed to get another £90 out of me in just a couple of months. I don't remember agreeing to this at all - I'm wondering if they simply added that charge to my account when I clicked within the app to download them.

The form to request a refund has a very tight character limit. If you select 'forgot to cancel' you are given an automated email saying they will not give you a refund. They might be allowed to do this - it might not be tehnically fraudulent - but don't be fooled, it is not easy to try for a week or two and just cancel. Look at the sheer number of complaints in the one star reviews about this exact thing. It's clearly in their business model - they are staying financially afloat by getting people to sign up to trial their app on £0.89 and then hitting them with multiple months worth of sky high outlandish fees. I've accidentally overpaid for other apps before with subscription fees - it's a very normal thing for folk with ADHD to do, and I often write it up as an 'ADHD tax' - but most of their competitors will let you at least reteroactively request a refund for 1-3 months if you haven't been using their app. And the cost for this is so much compared to any alternatives I've ever looked at or tried. I've lost maybe £10, £20 on an app like this before that I ended up not really using - but hey, worth it if I find something that actually works. But here... I quite literally lost near two hundred pounds on an app that I used for a week and thought I'd cancelled in the space of a couple of months. I don't even know if it is cancelled, I am going to take a note from the other folk here and block them with my bank too. 

Just download a gambling game instead, it'd be better for your mental health.

Oh and don't bother replying with that same copy and paste 'look at our help pages' that's under the other reviews. I've seen your help page. It's trash. You have my email if you'd like to help but you clearly don't.

title: Think you’ve tried everything?
body:

So I decided to let this trial of Fabulous into my life. It’s early days so far, and previous programmes have always felt a bit too new age and cringe-inducing. I’m trying to switch off the side of me that rejects this and instead embrace a different approach. 

And if you can do this, Fabulous is good. Even if as a Brit this does feel remarkably navel-gazy. I don’t want to bog myself down in therapy speak and there is definitely a happy medium. Fabulous seems so far to have found the right balance. Will update if I manage to last the journey.

body: I wanted to test this out on the free 7 day trial, but after a few days confirmed it wasn’t for me. I cancelled the subscription within 5 days, checked my Apple ID subscriptions to ensure it wasn’t there, and deleted the app. Then didn’t think any more of it. 4 months later I noticed the second of 2 bi-monthly charges, totalling £70 for an app I hadn’t used. In fact, an app that I could no longer log in to since I was “not a registered user” on either on my email addresses. Complaining to customer services I managed to get a refund for the second £35 charge only, leaving me £35 out of pocket. Extortionate rates for a habit app, with a lot of filler to labour the ‘scientific’ approach. Don’t get sucked in by the social media ads promising it’ll transform you into a better human. Don’t be tempted by the free trial. You will not find tangible benefit in the first few days, and you might be caught out like me on the daylight robbery rates.

body:

I have ADHD and life is bamboozling enough without this mess! Then it offers me 2 months at £34.99 which I declined, then half price, and now is offering me a year at £44! Make up your mind! 

Then, it’s trying to get me to add all the subscriptions to all the other apps that are connected. One was £70! body:

reported the app for review. 

This is a particularly egregious dark pattern from a company targeting users with ADHD, who are more likely to forget to immediately cancel and less likely to tolerate the frustration of jumping through hoops to do so. 

If you are struggling to retain users on value alone, then improve your app. This is perhaps the most unethical alternative possible. Shame on you.

title: Endless upsells and marketing
body:
I was led to believe this could be used as a basic free app and that adding a subscription for premium content was optional once you had got a feel for whether you liked the app, but this doesn’t seem to be the case.  I was made to fill in a series of tedious questions and then a pop up prompted me to pay before I could even look at the ‘personalised’ schedule and see if it is suitable for my needs.  There doesn’t seem to be a way round this, or if there is then it is well hidden. A countdown says that your “personalised” results will be saved for 15 minutes - presumably this has been deemed the optimal time for most people to dig out their credit card!

I am heartily sick of seeing ads for apps like this on social media and think apps that have to be paid for should state this up front.   There is zero point to filling in their forms (and sharing your personal information and email address for their marketing database) if all that it leads to is a demand for payment for something you have not tested.  Have seen this many times on everything from mindfulness apps to somatic yoga and wall Pilates and I now routinely hide and block anything that invites me to “take a 3 minute assessment” - ie share all my personal information with a company only interested in getting me to set up a direct debit 😡

title: Potentially life changing app, brings brightness in difficult days
body: When used regularly and often and following the habits that this app suggests and sets up and following the structure of the mountains that it gives you to conquer, starting with small habits and then a system of regular structured habits and then focusing on your goals, really sets up a great foundation to smash what you want to achieve and to get the most out of every day. In particular on difficult days the app can inspire and can change your mindset and give you new perspectives. I love the quotes from authors, poets, philosophers, scientists, great thinkers of our time that starts to embed in your mind when you read the coaching and the quotes and the journal prompts. The coaching sessions in particular are eloquent, magical, and inspiring, and the concept of you being on this journey through the fabulous landscape with all of the fabulous community there to support you is really a potentially life changing experience if used fully and regularly. The coaching sessions are read by brilliant eloquent speakers, a female and male voice, that poetically bring the writing to life. They definitely deserve recognition for that work recording the coaching sessions. It does take some commitment to use every day but it is well worth it.. I also wish it synced across my devices, as I have logged in on my iPhone but it is a completely different journey that I’m doing on there, so I just use my iPhone for the circles conversations)I wish there was support that you could contact to ask questions or to address these issues but I can’t find any email or support forms to fill in on the website or via the app. Thank you for creating this fabulous app!
author: JBaden

title: Quirky but effective
body: I’m loving this app. The concept of small consistent steps enabling the growth of new long term good habits has really worked for me. A lot of the coaching and activities ring bells with various studies and articles I’ve read over the years, but it’s great to have them all compressed in one place. I’ve now done a month and have completed the healthy eating journey and am midway through the energising journey and all going well. Admittedly it took me a wee while to fully understand how the app worked and to stick on one journey at a time - but once mastered its becomes such a useful tool. I also make use of the occasional bedtime story, I’m following the 8 week running plan, i do the 10 min stretch with friends when out on long walks and sometimes share a mediation with my daughter. If you want to improve your all round life It’s worth the effort of getting on top of this app and letting it help you mould a new path forwards. **** it’s been 2 months now and I’m still loving the app. Despite some health issues on the side I’ve list a stone through the healthy eating journey, have increased my exercise and flexibility through the daily stretch and walk nudges, have certainly improved the clutter in my flat ( still a work in progress) and am using the app to help me look at possibly changing careers by sue dung time each day working on some little side projects I’ve been procrastinating on fir years. Xxx Ok so it’s a year later and I totally fell off the app and the planet in the December lockdown!! So here I am back at round one, picking myself up again and appreciating the kindness in the app that’s helping me through it all. I notice a lot of updates from when I last did the first journey and they’re all really good. Makes the app easier to understand and more supportive. I’m interested and enthused about my journey but also about seeing how the app is progressing. All good stuff. Ps especially like the addition of nightly coaching. Fits my schedule and moods better. Xxx

title: Exploitative upselling
body:

In order to unsubscribe you need to find the email they sent when you first subscribed to find the link to unsubscribe. It is the hallmark of exploitation not to put the subscription in the AppStore so it can easily be managed and cancelled as every other decent app developer would. It makes cancelling difficult for a vulnerable group of people who are known to have executive functioning difficulties is verging on the criminal.

 I believe a class action by people defrauded by this app, trapped in multiple subscriptions they cannot cancel will be in this developer’s future. Message to developer: this is immoral behaviour and I am disgusted by you. Make it easy to cancel. Do not take money by profiting off people’s difficulties.

title: A good concept but here’s my experience -
body:
When you fill the questionnaire at the start it asks you things that you are already good at and areas you want to improve on (working out and eating healthily -and yes that includes water- were the areas I was strong in, procrastination, motivation and focus were areas I wanted to seriously work on). I was really excited to start the next day with tasks to get me more productive and focussed but the app only let me achieve drinking water and give me a well done if I said I drank a glass of water this morning. Guys, news flash lots of people have a water bottle on them at all times, we don’t need talking through it. Why not ask us if we drink enough water and if we drink it when we wake up? You’re wasting showing us what this app can really do if that’s what you get us to achieve first. 

You’re then told after signing up that you’re going to now get charged twice unless you cancel Apple subscription and when you go to cancel in the app (you’re asked to set up a profiler in google or Facebook so you have to message to cancel).  

If you want people to use your app, make it user friendly and actually tailor it to the initial questionnaire.

title: Really useful tool, bloated with different premium feature adverts
body:
I use fabulous as a timed tracker for my morning and evening routines. I have ADHD, so it really helps to have an app that’s following my routines in real-time with a timer so I don’t get distracted and lose track of time. It’s also a nice little dopamine rush to tick items off in the routine and hear the cute little achievement sound effects that play with it. What makes completing routines even more rewarding is the daily tracking feature the app has, where you can have running streaks that you can look back on. It doesn’t work so well for people with regularly changing schedules, but it’s still helpful.

The one thing I find annoying about Fabulous is that despite being a paying customer, I have to scroll past adverts for features of the app that I’m not interested in - for instance the real-life coaching. I already have an ADHD-specific coach, who I am happy with, and am also very happy using this app to track my routines. I don’t appreciate being bothered about paying for a Fabulous coach more than once.

Generally a really invaluable app for me that I would recommend to others, just a few niggles.

title: Money grabbing psychology at work
body:
This app seems to use multiple tricks to get you to pay before a proper free trial.

Here are just a few:
- If you sign up via the website, it will demand a minimum of $1 (and recommends around $16) to take a "free" trial that then renews at £34.99 every three months (so almost £150 a year).
- If you sign up via the Apple app, it's almost impossible to avoid the auto renewing subscription pop ups which actually does provide a real free trial. But oddly, this is only £34.99 a year, which means it's four times cheaper. Furthermore, if you sign up to a free trial via the App Store but have already created an account on the website, it signs you out of your account in the app.
- Pop up screens, reminder emails and other psychological tricks are sent constantly to either get you to sign up or renew. In fact, more effort seems to have been made on "growth hacking" psychological tricks to get your money rather than psychological tools to help you with your life.

In short, while the app is very aesthetically pleasing (and obviously companies need to pay their staff), I feel whoever is in charge of conversion rate optimisation is bordering on unethical practices to take money from their users BEFORE the app starts to provide any real value.

I think this is particularly egregious given that the people using this app are likely to have mental health issues or poor executive functioning. These people (of which I include myself) already struggle with forgetting to cancel numerous subscriptions, so this app simply adds another one to the list.

The only people I'd recommend this app to are unethical investors and greedy private equity firms. The recurring revenue from confused users will line their pockets.

If the founders or CEO really has any ethics, please fire whoever is doing your "growth hacking". They may be bringing in the cash, but I feel they are doing so unethically.

The app UI does seem nice, but use of dark patterns (manipulative design tactics used to influence user behaviour in ways that benefit the company, rather than the user) to deter cancellation of a psychology-backed habit-building app does not sit right with me.

title: Don’t bother.
body:
I had this for about 10 minutes, cancelled my subscription and deleted the app. 

I was sucked in by seeing a short quiz about ADHD types, as I feel I could be suffering with ADHD and SPD I thought I’d try it, more information I have the better whilst I’m building up the courage to talk to my doctor. 

I answered the questions and signed up to the 89p trial as I was more interested in the results of my answers, what I actually got was totally unexpected, unwanted and made me immediately hate the app. 

I was immediately forced into another quiz and asked a range of questions, answered this thinking they were baseline sign up questions and I’d see my results after. No such luck, instead I got pushed into a “journey” which I didn’t want. 

I already get outside professional help with my nutrition, exercise and mobility as well as I’ve recently undergone surgery; I didn’t ask to be set goals and the app asked nothing about me. I tried to browse around after I’ve got past the annoying amount of pop ups and again, nothing useful or any results from the first quiz I did. 

Also found it very rigid as it asked me what habits I already did… I selected one as there was no option to skip or say that I didn’t do any of the habits which would’ve been the truth. 

Rubbish app unless you fit into their perceived boxes, willing to follow their process with no question and have no issues with being told what to do and when.

title: Dreadful
body:
One of the most clunky and unintuitive apps I’ve seen on the store, this app asks you a seemingly never ending series of questions the first time you open it, so if you’re just curious and want to see what’s inside, you can’t do so until you hand over your email, create an account, and answer a whole lot of questions about your habits, and there isn’t a ‘back’ or ‘cancel’ option to stop the process. 

I gave up on the app and visited their website, to see what’s inside and whether I even want an account with them, but no, I couldn’t understand what the service was about until I created an account and logged in. On their website, somehow it seems I signed up for a free trial and a yearly subscription afterwards, but for the life of me I can’t figure out when that happened as their interface lacks transparency and is just absolutely overwhelming, you just can’t know where to find what. I contacted them when my credit card was charged, arguing that even if I agreed to the subscription accidentally, their interface is very misleading, lacks transparency, doesn’t let the consumer be properly informed and they don’t even send an email reminder or notification when the trial is about to expire and the credit card is going to be charged, so I was pretty clueless. I also didn’t see the subscription in my iPhone’s AppStore subscriptions list (apparently it only shows up on the web) otherwise I would’ve cancelled.

Anyway, Customer care declined to refund my payment even though I raised the issue within a couple of days and explained that they weren’t entirely transparent with me. So I have to now pay a hefty charge for an unintuitive app that I’m just not going to use because it causes me more stress than it resolves. Not to say everyone will have the same experience, but my personal opinion is that this app is too overwhelming to have the comforting effect and experience it’s meant to have.

title: Rigid, pushy, overwrought and borderline predatory
body: Tried a few habit trackers, mostly to try and find one that ties in with todos and general planning to keep on top of things. On top of that it’s completely tone-deaf to several things; anything around food it launches into weighing every day, fasting schedules and throwing out certain food groups that is absolutely inappropriate for anyone with ED backgrounds, with no warning. There’s an option when unsubscribing that you can find it “too female oriented when you’re male” which as a female that found the app patronising more than anything is just insulting. In summary, Fabulous is a mediocre habit tracker with a premium price tag, and even after subscribing you’re hounded to sign up for private coaching and to get more people signed up and promote the Instagram and buy X brand of item. The whole experience is unpleasant and I cannot recommend the app to anyone, when there are at least half a dozen options on the store that offer the exact same content, with more flexibility and streamlining, for much cheaper.

title: Truly Fabulous = Voice for everyone
body: I’ve just completed my first week using Fabulous. I’m really happy with the experience and am looking forward to working with the app throughout the year. Having said that, it’s unfortunate that the voice in the app has a distinct way of speaking that is potentially off-putting (like a permanently smiling yet impatient tourist). I would suggest having options for voices of different genders, ages in life and cultures, i.e. voices of colour. Otherwise, go with the global majority. There is a read-only option that silences the voice, but if Fabulous is trying to maximise accessibility or to create the impression of a coach who travels with you, then being able to select someone with whom you trust/identify would be really helpful. 4 stars. 🌟🌟🌟🌟

title: Being Neurodivergent Made This Difficult
body:
I do not wish this to come across as mean as I feel writing it, however, this app has some great ideas and, whilst I appreciate the effort clearly put in this is not a great app if you’re neurodivergent.

The app doesn’t take into account ADHD/Autism or other neurodiversities as there are some things that cannot be personalised in the way that’s required and can come off as super ableist.

For example, there is a journey all about improving organisation which I was intrigued by. However the entire thing is about writing down tasks in a notebook and ordering the most important three. This is something I’m not capable of as my mind doesn’t assign objective importance to tasks - that’s part of the disability - brushing my teeth can equally as difficult and important in my mind as going to work for 12 hours. Also being told to effectively write my tasks down to improve time management has the same energy as a ‘just use a planner - that’s what I do.’ 

Furthermore, due to being autistic, I need rigidity and structure and very specific instructions. ‘Eat a healthy breakfast’ is not useful, I need to have specific recipes, multiple options, etc. not to mention that whilst I am fortunate enough to not have an eating disorder myself, I can imagine something like this telling people to cut out sugar and drink water and remove easy, high calorie foods like biscuits, crackers, and other snack foods could be damaging. I need safe foods or else I won’t eat even if I’m hungry and want to eat. However it doesn’t take any other mental health or disability factors into account. I understand that is extremely difficult to do for everyone, however, as it advertises that it uses the best ‘behavioural science’ I can’t help but think that behavioural science is only the stuff relation to neurotypical, able-bodied, mentally healthy individuals and not allowing you to progress or having the coaching say things like ‘remember how it was chore to drink water when you started?’ And you’re still struggling but now you feel a lot like you’ve failed because this should be easy now, apparently, isn’t helpful to people with specific needs and requirements. 

I love the idea, and the people making it, clearly have put a lot into it, but please be careful if you’re disabled, having mental health issues, etc. as, even though it may work for you or even for a while, this app doesn’t take such things into account. With some more knowledge and a concept that understands that everyone has different needs, (and that water is not the only way to hydrate especially when there are reasons that’s not good for you, as an example) this could be really good. I may peek in again later to see if they have made any improvements but as it stands, it’s just not useful for me.

title: Avoid This App. You have been warned
body:
I was sent a special deal by email when I did not sign up for this app. I thought it was too expensive, but emails started coming into me with limited time offers. 
Finally an offer of a full year for only £20.99 came in!

It was clear that was the deal and I took screenshots that it was one years full subscription for £20.99.
I paid by PayPal taking further screenshots of the offer it was clear that this was NOT a trial period.

But it transpires they decided I was simply a person who is not going for expensive offers so they would rip me off by setting up an offer of £20.99 then when we have the payment details set up the high rate £34 per three months after only 12 days!
They get £20.99 and if it’s not notice get the rest of your money until you do.

This is actually just a scamming practice.

Now if you enjoy getting apps where there is no customer services, no contact except a form, who send emails with offers to get your payment details so they can charge a completely different fee of their choosing, followed by no ability to get refund, speak to anyone or any response then go ahead.

Fortunately I paid by PayPal so I could stop any further payments others have not been so lucky. However, I did not get a refund or the offer I was offered.
They don’t respond to PayPal either so that should tell you everything you need!

The contact details they have everywhere just run onto a standard form where you can’t get hold of anyone.

You should ask yourself before purchasing or buying this app if you have taken the precaution to read a reviews like mine and there is no customer services in 2022 is this really a company you want to deal with?

Like many others reviewing here have lost money… I wish I had read the reviews first… I hope this helps others avoid a lot of extra stress and hassle in your lives.

title: Careful if you struggle with ED/BDD
body:
I really wanted to like this app. I’m ADHD and struggle with housekeeping and finances and hoped Fabulous would help me create and sustain routines in those areas. I very intentionally did NOT list “healthy eating” as a goal because I have a history of disordered eating. Yet in the first five days of use, I’ve been told to drink water instead of pop, buy specific suggested breakfast foods, offered “easy healthy” breakfast ideas, read a motivational letter which used “quitting sugar” as an example, and prompted to get rid of “products that come in boxes or bags - like cookies, chips, and crackers”. The last *just* happened and that was when I knew it was time to unsubscribe and delete. 

The initial “journey” is NOT tailored to your needs and does NOT take your risk factors into consideration- not once did it ask about my history with diet and exercise, and clearly my telling it I’m happy with my current nutrition and movement had zero impact on what I was shown. 

There was also a really strange comment about buying a particular brand of water bottle because it’s BPA free that seemed very #sponcon but wasn’t marked as such in any way.

title: Wanted to like it but too many issues in the first week
body:
Update:

This app caused me the most financial stress I can ever have. 

I cancelled the subscription due to the stress described below, 

Only to find out just now that they have charged me TWICE in 3 days for Yearly subscription when I don’t even have the app. 

I am fuming 

// 

Got the app after quite a few months of considering it. Kudos for the team , there is lots of potential and I really wanted to enjoy it but have had more stress navigating it around and with the subscription than enjoyment :( As a whole - I found it very overwhelming. I tried creating a morning routine with different habits - the alarm did not work; none of the habits would pop as a reminder in the morning but it will appear more after the time would have passed. The mood check in - popped at random Times of the day and I could not find it on my own to put in my mood if I wanted to. It seems to offer too many things at once and too little control to adapt thing your way :(( On the side I also had problems with the free trial and subscription - I cancelled it when the free 7 days ended. Upon cancellation, they offered a 30 day free trial and I chose it and yet the app still charged me. When I tried to cancel it / contact the team - it cancelled my free premium trial and I still haven’t gotten a refund for the years plans. So all in all it’s been more hassle than it’s worth :(

title: Nice Idea, Appalling User Experience
body: At its heart this app has a good idea - but the user experience is appalling. Multiple menus within menus, endless barrage of reminder and marketing emails, confusing sub-sections within subsections that make the app a nightmare to navigate, messages from other ‘users’ that are clearly sent by bots, and motivational messages that endlessly (and needlessly) quote famous authors as if literary pretentiousness is a substitute for insightful comment. Worst of all, the app seems incapable of integrating the web version of Fabulous with the App Store version, so I was constantly being bumped out of the Premium version and asked to pay again. When I tried to re-initiate my membership I ended up getting charged twice. The company did finally refund, but it took a long time and multiple emails and form fills. By which point I’d lost my patience with the company. Apparently the integration between the app and web version has been fixed, I’m not sure I’ll be bothering to find out.

title: Good idea, bad user experience
body:
I’m a pretty productive and busy lead stakeholder in a tech start up. I was looking for an app that can compartmentalise my self-improvement from my work tasks. I thought Fabulous looked good but, oh my, what a ridiculously over-thought user experience it was.

When I tick anything off I am met with some stupid cut scene that I can’t imagine ANYONE asked for (guys I drank some water, I didn’t circumnavigate the globe…CHILL ALREADY). I can never find what I’m looking for and it keeps trying to shove new things on me instead of letting me explore and discover in a nice and easy way. The pop ups and suggestions are literally the lost aggressive I’ve seen from an app.

I’ve tried it for a few days but I’ll be deleting it now. All I wanted was something that can help me plan goals and reach them whilst giving me some half decent encouragement, this is just way too much

Is it a game? Is it an app? Is it a self-improvement system? It doesn’t seem to know. 

I honestly can’t think who this is for. Place simplify your user journey. It is mental

title: Nice idea but not tailored to you
body:
This seemed like a good idea so I signed up. First fail; it asked me for my age then gave me a bland exercise program completely unsuitable - possibly harmful if I had done it. Another app I have takes a more responsible approach and tailors suggested exercises to my age, fitness level and any issues I flag, which is the safe and healthy way to do it. If I had followed any of these exercise routines it would have damaged my self esteem too. 

Next; the interface is cluttered and messy. A simpler drill down layout would be cleaner to use.

Thirdly, the graphics were not to my style. I prefer real images eg a forest rather than animations.

Regarding payment; the app offered me one weeks trial then pay for a year. The annual price is good if you find the app useful it’s a bargain; however a years subscription after one week of trialling it wasn’t long enough for me to find something about it that I liked enough so I cancelled it.

Summary; good idea but not tailored to you. It seems the developers have intentions to help but providing generic exercise routines without tailoring options is dangerous. Dumbed down almost patronising. 

It seems to help some people which is good.

title: Beautiful app terrible pricing model
body:
This is an absolutely gorgeous app. The UI is crisp, detailed and so incredibly well thought out. It’s obviously taken a great deal of time and money to develop.

 I’m currently trialling it and genuinely would like to continue. My main gripe is the fact that only one pricing model is offered. 

 This led me to cancel DURING the trial and continue to assess the value of app without risking the rather hefty £35+ payment. 

 Dev’s please consider a less aggressive tiered pricing model. You offer a genuinely lovely app, but you’re doing so at a time when the economy is cratering and peoples wallets are shrinking. 

 Please rethink your model and offer a monthly payment option and a discounted annual tier. I AM considering the upgrade but felt the need to cancel prior to renewal to ensure the choice is mine and is not automated.

title: Promising… but needs work
body:
I used subscribed to Fabulous’ annual plan but decided to delete the app after 9 weeks.

It has a really nice central idea for an app - build better habits - and some of the design work is beautiful and very inspiring. 

There are two main problems with the app that make it fundamentally unusable in the long-term: 

1. The UI is exceptionally cluttered. The central feature of the habit tracker is buried beneath layers of coaching videos, daily poems, social “circles”. The clean, simple idea at the heart of the app is lost amidst a bunch of other ideas that seem to have just been thrown in (and without much care or design time, at that). 

2. The routines the app helps develop are overly-prescriptive. I.e. Fabulous makes it so that you will develop the routines that Fabulous thinks are best for you. At first, this is helpful as the habits are exceptionally broad (e.g. drink water immediately upon waking up every morning) but not everyone necessarily wants to “eat a fabulous breakfast” or meditate. 

I feel a bit harsh at giving a rating of only 2 stars but I think it’s appropriate as the app really isn’t yet developed enough to do what it needs to. I’d encourage the developers to look at apps like DuoLingo to see how a clean, simple interface can work in a coaching app.

title: Letting me follow their way
body:
It may be too early to clearly know the full potential of the app.  

Since I started with the application I decided to focus on my life, making more time than I previously had, simply by not wasting it. I have ADHD, and schedules aren’t my strength. 😅

I use SleepCycle to track my sleep and wake me up when my sleep is in the lightest moment, then I switch app to @Fabulous. Apart from reminding me to drink a glass of water when I wake up followed by some deep breathing exercises, I do few steps helped with my smartwatch Garmin Venu to start the day in a positive way and see how I improve my health in long term. I'm doing 10 minutes of cardio exercises, 16 minutes running (2.5 kms), on the way back I turn on the kettle, I take a shower, I get dressed, I have a great breakfast as Fabulous suggests and in an hour and a bit, I'm ready for action. Just today I got a bit distracted writing a review, I promise I will keep on track. 😄

Thank you Fabulous for giving me a tool to rearrange my life and give a bit of order. 🙌🏼🫂

I paid for the premium version for a year.  

For people who are searching for jobs. They are recruiting and have some cool positions, just saying. 😉

title: Fabulous!
body:
Good review:

It’s a great app that shows short animations and videos to show Guide you through your that path you take. If you complete a Target you get a feeling of achievement and it gives you a good well done. They use inspirational letters and rewards to keep you going.

Improvements: 

Obviously it is a good app but there are a few things I think it would make the app easier and better to use! 
- multiple notifications for a task that is set 
- a tutorial at the start of how to use the app
 
Overall review:

I think that app is a great app and it makes amazing results when you get the hang of how to use it. It’s good for all ages and sets good habits in at a young age; even if you are older it’s good to learn new ways and this app is perfect for this. I downloaded many other apps before this app and they are all useless in comparison . You can get a premium pack where you unlock different features however it is certainly not needed so if you can’t afford it I wouldn’t worry. But it is fantastic to have. You have lots of features that you don’t have to unlock using the premium buy but it is worth getting the premium pack and paying the money.  Overall this is a fantastic app that will help you get rid of bad habits and get onto good habits. Definitely get this app and check it out.

title: Confusing interface, makes me worse
body:
I really want to love this app, it started so well asking me questions and promised a tailored experience. 

But the UI is just so confusing for me, each icon at the bottom leads almost into 5 separate apps each with their own random layout and navigation.   Trying to find anything just isn’t logical for me.   Trying to find what I’m supposed to do for my “tailored” program is impossible. 

The app consistently fails to remind or track my routines, so to catch up is convoluted way and you can’t add more than one missed thing in a row, each time you add a missed one you get interrupted by a splash screen. 

The app doesn’t ask what time I want reminders to fit in with my routine, instead it interrupts me at random times that I inevitably dismiss it and therefore miss out on whatever it is trying to help me with. 

I’ve had to cancel because this is simply making me worse, it is adding complexity to my life at a time I need to simplify, declutter, get motivated and stay on track.

title: Awful service and a dishonest company!
body:
I haven’t found the app of any use. I initially signed up to a free 7 day trial, which I then got sent an email by fabulous offering to extend it to a 30 day trial. After around 2 weeks I realised this app really wasn’t working for me and wasn’t worth the £35 annual subscription by a long shot so tried to cancel the app through iTunes subscriptions. Where I then saw they had charged me the annual subscription cost after 7 days emailed 2 weeks 6 days after signing up on iTunes to complain and query why subscription payment was taken even though email had offered it was extending free trial to 30 days. I sent this email on 14th October and received no reply until the 4th December!!! Now they tell me I’ve been charged twice (on iTunes AND through the website offering to extend the 7 day trial up to 30 days) and that they will only refund one subscription (iTunes) even though I emailed them within the 30 days telling them I wanted to cancel subscription!! They say as it’s now out of the 30 day trial they won’t honour that refund (even though I emailed them within the 30 days) I’m now collating all the dates, emails, offer etc. and escalating this higher and seeking legal advice under the trade descriptions act. 
Overall a dreadful service from a company that have clearly used misleading emails to garner subscriptions. Do not sign up to this app under any circumstances…..it’ll be a world of hassle, waste of money and a dreadful company to do business with!

title: Tried lots of others before
body:
I’ve been trying to find something which would help me focus better and, although it’s only been a week so far, this is looking really good.
It started at too basic a level for me (drink a glass of water every morning, have breakfast every day) but I decided not to jump forward and I’m glad I didn’t.
I’ve always known the life I want needs discipline and focus so I decided to be disciplined enough to do stuff that I thought I was already doing.
I’ve now realised they weren’t habits, they were things I did most of the time but, crucially, stopped them at the times I needed them most.

title: I cannot afford to feed my kids and I now
body: Since this deceiving app took my money, without my consent, I am left with £30 to feed my kids and I for a month. I can’t afford to pay the heating and electricity bills as it is. I tried to cancel the subscription but it was no use, they still took the little money I had left. I was a minute in to using the app, and before I got a chance to even read the page, (it changed quickly without an option) .. they had charged me £36 (for after the free trial) by using the Touch ID (which my thumb happened to be on the home button as I was about to double click it to open a different app). I had no warning whatsoever and the app itself didn’t make it clear that I had to PAY! I didn’t expect I’d be charged for an app that is supposedly offering ‘support’. Out of my monthly wages, after I have paid my rent, I am left with £70. I do my very best but I am struggling massively as it is. My kids and I use candles instead of electricity as we can only afford £5 electricity a month, which lasts about 3 days. We use lots of blankets and cuddle up together to stay warm as we can’t afford to heat the house either. So we are then left with £65 for food to last a month. I am hungry most of the time and often, my kids get hungry too.  Since this app has robbed £36 from me, I am terrified as to how we are going to survive this month, we will starve. So thankyou for that. What a “fabulous” app this is. It left me with 10X the amount of anxiety I already had, which was enough as it was. I am scared and I am scared for my kids. Shame on you.

title: I wanted to like this
body:
I really wanted to like this, but have so many issues with it that I can’t carry on. 

First, the graphics are twee beyond belief. 

Second, this is really incompatible with parenting. They have a lovely animation about a “new Mum” going for a run and pushing though and it making her feel amazing. I’m so glad I didn’t find this app when I actually was a new Mum because that was not my lived experience. I would have been gaslit as anything. Even now with school aged kids, their suggestions for the number of things I’m meant to do immediately when I get up are wholly unrealistic. 

On a similar note, this is ableist as anything. So I would avoid it if you have any long term health issues.

Ultimately though it was the relentless, almost cult-like, positivity that really got to me. I’m not trying to change my habits because I’m under some delusion they’re going to fundamentally alter my life (or my actual self, as they audaciously imply). I’d like to change my habits to try to support my mind and body in functioning better in a fundamentally quite dysfunctional world. Fabulous doesn’t seem to have any space for that level of nuance. 

As I say, I desperately wanted to like and use this. I would have happily handed over chunks of cash if it was actually useful. But as a parent with less than stellar mental health, Fabulous made me feel gaslit. Not a fabulous outcome.

title: Good ideas, poor execution
body:
I have now been using the app for a few weeks and no, I was not „tricked“ into paying - it was my intention to be a paying customer. 
Whilst I love the idea of the app, there is a lot that only seems to work in the first week to draw you in and then gets reduced to what is essentially a list with items to tick off. The nice poems stopped after the first week. The landscape through which you progress each week is only visible in the morning when you completed your routine and doesn’t do anything. So the little figurine with which they seem to have wanted you to identify or at least connect in some way, loses its job. I would have loved to have that map as a starting point, where I can look into previous days, re-listen to previous coaching sessions and get that feeling of going through different levels in a game. 
The Journey tab is just blank now and nothing comes up. Not sure what’s up with that. 
It is completely unclear what purpose the Launch tab has. I suspect the journey part of it should actually be available under the journey section. The „make me fabulous“ also doesn’t work properly- the sections „fabulous creed“ and „ambience“ just have that „it’s loading“ circle of death there but are inaccessible. 
And whilst the idea of having circles is nice, it is a useless feature because you cannot properly interact with other users. No way of @-ing someone let alone send a dm, so if someone leaves a comment under your comment you will never know unless you scroll aaaaaaaall the way back to that post regularly to check the replies. The admins also don’t interact with users, only post some „tell us about…“ stuff and never look back at it. 
Where the design works, it is beautiful; my favourite being the ambience music in the background. 
But overall, it looks like someone had 5 different design ideas that got jumbled together and never got ironed out to create the app it has the potential to be.

title: Not a great UX
body:
Couldn’t get on board with the UX at all. 

1) I came to the app from an Instagram Ad and when I went to log in it wanted me to complete the whole questionnaire I’d just completed again with no option to skip and log in using the account I’d just created. This was frustrating as it’s a lengthy questionnaire.

2) Once I was in the app there were way too many tool tips. I feel like this is just a craze with UX designers right now thinking every user needs hand holding through an app. Some people, like me, prefer to push buttons and see what happens, so I found the tool tips very frustrating. You’re simply trying to have a look around and tool tips fly up and won’t disappear until you complete the task they’re guiding you through. There should be an option to turn these off.

On a positive note, that actual UI of the app looks great. It’s clear a lot of work has gone into this app. But, for me the annoying tool tips and ill thought out user journey make it too irritating. If you like apps that hand hold you with tool tips through tasks as simple as hitting a check mark, it might be for you.

title: Great app, but UX + UI needs consistency
body:
I’ve found it very helpful and simple to motivate small changes that are fundamental to a healthy lifestyle, both physical and mental.

The one thing I notice continually is the app feels like it’s been ‘made from a few different Lego bricks’ -

1.  It can be a little confusing when tasks are completed exactly how to complete them, or how to accept further tasks. Task flows can sometimes lead you to a video where you accept a new challenge, but you have to input data (“I’ve drunk water for day 3”) on another state, which takes you to a slightly different task flow. This can be resolved by crafting a core task flow pattern, and rinse and repeating.

2. It would be great to see more consistency in UI components / look and feel. I’m unsure if you have a design system already, but creating cohesion between states and task flows will make the experience feel like a contained, singular environment rather than multiple evolutions of designs bolted on together.

I feel this would be a natural iteration of the great experience + intention that’s already going behind the app.

However, I think it needs a way for users to specify if there are journeys and challenges that we wish to avoid or to specify dietary preferences. One example would be that I’m vegan and it told me to eat buy and eat eggs which is a small problem, but should be easy to avoid with some personalisation. 

What worries me more is that after completing my first week it invited me to a weekly carb-cutting challenge. I declined as I recovered from an eating disorder a few years ago and these kinds of challenges and journeys would not be helpful to me. I’ve looked to see if there is a way to personalise recommendations that takes these preferences into account but can’t seem to find a way. It would be reassuring to know that I can continue to use this app without repeated pressure to follow a specific diet or restrict foods.

The only one that I’ve come across that cancels everything once you cancel the subscription is Apple TV it will not let you have the free features without the subscription. title: Very good at some things, awful at others
body:
Giving this app three stars feels a bit harsh, but I thing 4 would be generous. 

The app is really good for helping set up solid routines to get you into the right headspace for certain portions of your day. I have always been somebody who has a morning routine, sleep routine... but found myself struggling to commit to them lately. This app has massively helped with that and throughout the day. 

However the meditations in this app are so terrible, they often aren’t actually even guided meditations just monologues. It also uses guilt tactics in some of the letters/daily coaching. It just feels like in portions of the app people with experience in mindfulness/therapy weren’t consulted in the slightest. The letters are often overly negative, focusing on what the worst situation could be if you continue in your ways before switching the narrative. However the majority of the time is devoted to describing in detail this negative behaviour. Ignoring the fact that shame and guilt are often reasons people continue with a negative behaviour... 

So I find myself, opening this app and then switching to other apps for guided meditation/coaching. 

I have high hopes for this app, as the concept is brilliant. Fixing portions of the content would improve it immeasurably.

surely it would be smarter to be providing education to users through articles or videos about food timing and calorie awareness rather than giving a blanket answer to their weight loss woes.

My main criticism is that the app constantly asks for feedback, like this review, I’ve only done so in the hope that it will stop asking me for one. You also get the feeling that the developers just want you to share everything with everyone to encourage new users and grow numbers. I understand this is pretty standard these days, however with this type of app it feels a little disruptive to the personal experience and is removing some of the enjoyment. On the whole though, it’s pretty good. Will see where it takes me.

title: Has improved my mood
body: I have struggled with depression since my early 20s and I’d tried Fabulous before but never gave it a true chance. Having a routine is so important for our mental well being now more than ever and the app is designed so well to instil good self care. It starts simple so you can manage the tasks and gives helpful tips and information along the way. This app gives you such a range of resources there really is something for everyone. When you first start using it, it will ask you about what you want to focus on to improve on your journey, another lovely personal touch.  I’m now building a routine for 21 days but if I manage to stick to it I maybe investing in the premium version. Fabulous makes it so easy for me to be proactive about self care which is what I personally require. I’ve tried other well being apps but this one is definitely a cut above the rest.

body:

However, way to many screens which are confusing initially to click through, in terms of where I should be going with my journey through the app. Also the blue used extensively is too much for me personally especially on the FAQ pop ups. This along with the purposeful slow speed text content loads on the FAQ, makes the app slightly frustrating to use and put me off.

However, that been said if you are new to habits and looking for improvement in your life this app definitely has all the right tools for you! Once you get past the initial overload and work out what’s what, you will definitely see improvement in your life!

title: Manipulative marketing
body: During sign up, you’re asked if you want to agree to receiving notifications. The options are “Yes, I want to succeed” or “No, I’ll do this on my own”. Rather than giving a good reason to agree to notifications, the developer chose to manipulate us by framing rejecting notifications as rejecting their attempt to pursue a life of well-being. title: They just take your money
body:
I signed up for the 7 day trial and was going to cancel on the 7th day. I woke up to find money taken from my account. I never consented to joining premium and there were no notifications that I needed premium to continue to use the app. I am disappointed. While the Fabulous app developers may have done something legal, it is financially predatory and unethical. 
The service “auto renewed” a payment plan that I did NOT consent to in the first place and they take money from your account if you don’t unsubscribe using your iTunes account at least 24 hours before they intend to charge. This is not made clear in the terms and conditions. Moreover, unsubscribing from the app does not mean they won’t charge you. I am very disappointed with this predatory financial plan and hope the developers will design business ethics that are in line with the “fabulous” ethos they intend to coach their users into mastering.

title: Useful so far
body:
I’m reviewing after using the app for a week, so it’s possible I’ll wish I’d rated it more highly once I’ve seen more of what it can do - but since it is already asking for a review, here it is.
I’ve found the app useful. It starts off getting you to drink water as soon as you wake up for 3 days in a row, and builds other habits from there. So far I’m drinking water, eating a good breakfast, and doing a simple workout 3 times a week. The effects of this aren’t clear yet as it’s still early days. However, it’s already improved my mental state and attitude towards routine. 
The app is very aesthetically pleasing, and I think a lot of people would enjoy the visual appeal. I personally find the interface a bit overwrought and would actually prefer a much simpler layout and format, without all the distracting sections and narrative frills. However, it’s clear enough to keep me coming back. 
I am going to keep using the app and, as things stand at the moment, I would sign up for the paid version. There’s a lot of work that’s gone into it, and the early results are promising.

title: App with Huge Potential
body:
Early days for me but really like it overall. Seems to use very evidence-based approach to forming good habits and virtuous circles of self-care, couched in a questing story format that’s very compelling and effective.

Constructive criticisms: 

Tone would probably be a little off-putting if you’re not one or more of the following: traditionally “feminine”, New Age-y, have a camp/ postmodern sense of humour which allows you to enjoy elements that might otherwise be off-putting (e.g. lots of illustrations of floaty, glamorous women that look like they come from a particularly naff set of Tarot cards).

The above also gives the impression that sooner or later I’m going to be exposed to some serious woo-woo. Really hope that’s not the case. 

Accordingly, a slight feel of amateurishness and clunkiness in the overall design.

Really need a professional poet to work on the awful doggerel used in some of the story-telling. Really, really naff and ugly and off-putting if you love poetry.

title: Annoying and alarms don’t work
body:
Hey,

At first I really wanted this to be good and its ok. I’ll give a few points;

Pros
1. Design is nice. Reminds me of that game Journey from PS store. 
2. Nice concept, like the little wins on each completed tasks.

Cons
1. Too many cut scene things. Bloody annoying. I want to do my routine thing and then do something else. Especially at the start of setting these routines, I am not wanting to spend 10 mins on some screen that the sound isn’t working on when it says, use headphones. 
2. You need headphones on to hear/understand the majority of things happening. I don’t have sound on my phone usually during work etc. 
3. Everything takes so long. Long scenes, pushing me to buy constantly even though I have never used the app, lots of little middle screens that don’t need to be there, the list goes on. 
4. Asks you to set alarms, but doesn’t work with iPhone alarms so they never go off :(
5. You have only focused on good design, not good experience. That frustrates me.

If you have patience, this app is perfect for you. I just want to check that I have done it and continue with my day.

title: Great idea terribly executed
body: The thinking behind this app is great and definitely something I could get behind and I would tell everyone I know about it...if it worked. Unfortunately the app is glitchy as all hell and developers don’t appear to have done anything to fix that over the past eight months (I first subscribed last December, got fed up with the glitches and ditched it after a few months, then returned a few weeks ago to see if the user experience had been improved but sadly nope). Notifications happen at random and don’t necessarily have any connection to what you’ve *actually* been up to. And god forbid you join a challenge because it seems to be pot luck as to whether you will bet get rid of it again (regardless of whether you complete it). As with other reviewers, I agree there should be more flexibility earlier on in the journey to personalise it to whatever level you are at / needs you have. I once read a note from one of the creators in response to the app being labelled as not particularly intuitive or user friendly, claiming it was ‘like an instrument’ that you play around with to figure out how to make the music you want or something - which in the nicest possible way just sounds like a complete cop out rather than actually addressing feedback. I really hope the developers listen to feedback and genuinely work to improve this app, because as I said at the start, it genuinely has bags of potential. It’s just frustratingly lacking at the moment and hasn’t shown any improvement, which unfortunately makes it look like a money spinning scheme rather than an app designed to help people, with their needs at the centre of things.

title: I’m glad I forgot to cancel 😂
body:
So yeah, lots of negative reviews about getting “trapped” in the annual subscription. I knew what I was getting into when I signed my free trial. It was very clear. I was then too lazy to set a reminder to cancel. Didn’t touch the app until after the week was up and realised I had paid. But hey, that’s my wrong doing, I signed a contract and promised to pay! 

So I thought I may as well try it now, given I’m committed to a year, and voila! That commitment has now turned into a total love for this app. Had it been a monthly subscription, my emotional investment wouldn’t have been so strong. 

As a life coach I download every habit app known to man, and this is by far the most compelling. Some people benefit from the hand holding. I’m one of them, because I’m the most humanist of flawed humans. I tend to focus on the big successes and forget the tiny details. I love how enjoyable and rewarding this app is to use. It uses positive reinforcement instead of guilt, like most habit apps. It gives you positive experiences even within the app. 

The “journey” is also important, as the unique phases of building a habit have unique challenges and obstacles that need to be addressed uniquely in order to keep momentum. It’s this level of detail, and the interactivity and extremely pleasant user experience that makes it worth the money to me. 

Some may find this overwhelming as it is very prompting and challenges you to add more and more. It has to suit where your personality is right now. So I would recommend *actually* using the week trial to get that momentum. And set a reminder on your phone the day before you need to cancel, in the case it’s not for you :) but I’m sure it will be for many more!

title: Brilliant
body:
I am updating my review based on app usage -
The app has slowed right down, it is basically unresponsive, which is really frustrating.

It lets you tick off your tasks then randomly deletes all the ticks again, I have deleted it and downloaded it again. Updated it, updated my phone and it’s still reacting terribly, definitely can’t type notes into it anymore or discover new things; it just crashes. None of my other apps are crashing or struggling to function, it’s just this one.

Very disappointing for the £36 it cost! 

I’ve downloaded endless versions of life planning apps and none of them have stuck for longer than a few days. Fabulous has a great layout, I love that you can join challenges and speak to others completing the same challenge. 
I never thought I would spend money on an app like this but I loved it after the first week free trial. The style and flexibility of the tasks you can add/ creating your own personal tasks is great. I feel like it is making me into a more productive person. I just hope I can continue with all of my productivity when lockdown is over and I return to work!

title: Okay, That Notification Needs To Go
body:
I love this app, it’s beautiful and easy to use. The music is also really top notch when I’m reading, and as long as I don’t listen to the narrator- I love the stories and artwork. However, there is a notification that I woke up to this morning saying, ‘hey, it’s you 10 years from now. I’m still the same person I was, I haven’t changed.’ Haha. What?! All because I hadn’t woken up to drink water? That was just patronising and quite frankly, unnecessary. 

I would say the developers needs to reevaluate that bit. As a further matter, I’ve always drank water as soon as I wake up, so it would be nice if the app maybe asked a few questions to sort out where users are at from the start... You might get better retention that way as well... Perhaps then you’ll not need those strange shaming tactics!

title: DO NOT BUY THIS APP UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCES!!!
body: DO NOT BUY THIS APP UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCES! They have misled me into buying a subscription that I cannot afford. I am extremely good with subs but this app MISLED me into believing that I would be paying a monthly subscription. I didn’t think much of the app to begin with but I thought I would give it a go and I didn’t mind paying for one month more since the app implied that it would be a monthly fee. I was therefore shocked and appalled to find this morning that £35.99 had been taken out of my bank account. I found an email address for the app and submitted a request for a refund  but got an automated response. I then submitted a complaint through the app (as I was told to) which emailed me with another automatic response with a link for a reimbursement. The form it sends however offers NO possibility of a reimbursement. THIS APP IS A CON! I cannot get over how misleading it is and there is no number to call anyone and I am sure some automated response to this complaint will say, ‘sorry to hear about this! please email us!’ which will lead down the same awful rabbit hole. I will continue to try and get my money back as £35.99 is way too much and I can’t afford it. I am shocked by this app and I hope no one supports them.

The constant nudges to invite and challenge other people was really irritating.  I accidentally ticked that I’d taken my medication one day and discovered that you cannot undo a task ticked off by mistake (this, in my opinion is worrying). 
I’ve stopped using the app now and I feel like a weight has been lifted from my shoulders, I’m no longer tying myself up in knots trying to keep up with random challenges or making pinky promises with my phone to go and drink a glass of water.

title: Don’t forget to cancel your subscription before the trial week expires!
body:
Awful app and customer journey. Poor gamification, a lot of limitations. I wish I had read the comments before I installed the app, as I see a lot of people had a similar dissatisfying experience with it. 
Don’t get tricked into a full year subscription (£36). If it happens, the app will have only negative emotions associated with it. The customer service lacks the basic interest in customer satisfaction and retention. You may be fabulously ignored. Needless to say there was no empathy at all, considering the current pandemic situation and lockdowns worldwide. Also, when I tried to cancel the subscription via the app, the cancellation could only go through if I submitted my email and agreed to have a 20-min interview with a behavioural economist, which is an unreasonable post sale barrier. They say it’s optional, but it’s not. You can cancel it only through your Apple account subscriptions. What they could’ve done differently - offer a partial refund or a discount or a longer subscription period, anything would be better than just in other words saying “it’s your fault”, I would accept it as sunk cost and give it another try maybe. 
There an absolutely great app - Calm. I bought a lifetime subscription to it - worth every penny. Can’t say the same about not so fabulous “Fabulous” app.

title: Chocolate teapot
body:
It’s a beautiful looking app and a great idea, but the severe lack of flexibility reduces it to being about half as useful as taking a pen and paper and making your own list of goals. 

I don’t mind the free trial followed by automatic annual charge (Yes it’s a bit of a money grab, but I feel like this is standard procedure now and it’s made clear when signing up) 

The first goal is drinking water when you wake up... It lasts for three days and is unavoidable. It doesn’t seem like I’m able to add/edit my goals in the meantime? In my case I already drink water in the morning, and I don’t fancy waiting three days to unlock the next one (which just seems to be having a healthy breakfast?!) when I’ve been doing this for years. This inflexibility seems really bizarre to me... Shouldn’t I be able to set relevant goals and ignore those that aren’t relevant? 

It’s such a shame because all the tools are in the app! The ideas, the graphics, the design etc etc, but benefits have been made so inaccessible 😩 I’d have been more than happy to pay a yearly sub but now I’m cancelling my subscription the day I downloaded. On the plus side, this should be a fairly simple fix for developers. If I haven’t found an alternative, I’ll definitely be checking in the future to see if it’s changed. 

Thanks for reading!

Looks pretty - but merely a diary with some pretty stuff and advice you have probably already googled.... and if you really need this, I suggest you save your money for some actual coaching sessions when that can be arranged. title: Run by seemingly ignorant yuppies from hell
body: Absolutely appalled. Wasn’t interested in the app after using the trial. Turned off auto renewal and then was charged for a FULL YEAR. Interestingly, it was advertised as ‘£3 a month, £36.99 a year’ which is a scam in itself, as you are not charged monthly whatsoever, and I don’t even think there is even an option for that. Under the guise of bettering people’s lives, you could actually be preventing vulnerable people who can’t afford to spend their money on expensive self-help apps from buying food during, I don’t know, the CORONAVIRUS. EPIDEMIC. I couldn’t sleep last night after I saw the money come out of my account. I have about £50 to my name and don’t know how I’m making it through the weeks. I spent 30 minutes trying to file for a refund only to have Apple make me write a description and then send me an automated message that ‘I do not meet the requirements for a refund’ which is utter bull in itself. On other subscription platforms there are up to 2 weeks of cool down period after the purchase to claim a refund. When buying clothes or any service, if you are unhappy with what you are provided or are unable to afford it, you are entitled as a customer to get your money back. You don’t even have a customer service email address which is suspicious in itself. Now I feel the need to use the app so not to waste it but all it will do is leave me with a bitter taste in my mouth which I don’t think is doing much for my mental health. Thanks a lot guys, changing the world one step at a time.
