As for the reviews claiming this is a scam,
it is very clear that after the free trial you will be charged, people seem annoyed because they forgot to cancel before the free trial ended. If you did not cancel before the end of the trial period I do not see how you can blame the developers, this is something you signed up to. You have to cancel through your Apple ID settings, but this is the same for all subscription based apps I have used.

As for me I payed the yearly subscription and this has been worthwhile. It may be somewhat pricey but for myself personally the beautiful designs in the app are what I'm paying for. Sure you can find cheaper or free alternatives to check of your habits, but for myself using something that looks great helps me coming back each day :)

title: Good idea, terrible sales user journey
body: This app was suggested to me as I use elevate which I enjoy. I tried it and I thought it was ok, but stopped using after a couple of days. While it does say the yearly subscription fee on purchase, I did intend to cancel. I was a couple of days late and forgot to do so and there is no way to cancel there after and was charged the annual £36. I think this is a horrible business model and I have now lost trust in this developer. I really think there should be a less harsh payment system for this. So many people have fell for the same trap and it really is a horrible feeling, especially when your not actually using the app. This is not a sustainable way to treat potential customers who are not sure if they want to commit. It’s also completely hypocritical to design an app that’s about improving your daily habits and positive mental state, by making people feel conned and ripped off. Surely you want to build a brand based on trust and customer loyalty, not just a bunch of one off payments by people that never recommend it and actually advise against using it. Sort it out, make a cooling off period, and don’t continue like this, it’s horrible.

title: Why’s everyone so mad?
body:
It’s only day one but so far I’m loving this app! I read all the reviews and was like woah this sounds so dodgy i better be careful what i click on. But after going on the app it’s pretty clear what to do. But maybe some people aren’t familiar with subscription apps, because i knew exactly what to do to ensure i didn’t get renewed... even though it clearly states a step by step of how to do it on the subscription area? 

Also everyone’s so annoyed at the water thing! I think it’s a perfect way to start off! You can’t have day one doing yoga, drinking 3 smoothies and a marathon 😂 that has no longevity to it. I really like the principle of building that foundation. 

I know it’s kinda pricey for an app. But it’s also pricey for a personal trainer, a therapist etc. These are just some investments that are worth making. I’d rather get this than another coat or something. 

I have a mental health journal i keep, and i pretty much track all these things. So having both with really compliment one another. I’m really excited to see where it goes. 

Anyway I’ll finish my trial and see where i stand but so far I’m liking what it has to offer. 🥰

body:

The reminder feature which is free on my phone can essentially do the same thing. 
I went to cancel the subscription but got there one day too late so it has cost me £55!!! A year’s subscription?!
So I wrote to them and got an automated reply saying contact Apple.
I contacted Apple and also got an automated reply telling me how to cancel a subscription... I can for December 2020!!! I could have cried. That’s a few hours wages down the drain!

I only want to hear back from the developers if it will be to tell me they will refund me 11 months of the subscription. Thanks.

title: This app is a turnaround.
body:
I’ve struggled with anxiety and depression for several years, and the hardest problem has been hating using my phone because of all the negative things that come from it. Social media, pictures of yourself, screen time in general, so on. However, finding a good routine has forced me to use my phone often: for calendar, reminders, notes, etc. This much screen time inevitably led me to gravitate toward using those parts of my phone that I don’t like so much. With Fabulous, I am able to use it to the bare minimum, as it combines everything I need to properly formulate a healthy structure to my day, without using multiple apps and spending an awfully large amount of time doing so. Fabulous brings everything together in a really useful way: the visuals are pleasing, the audio is soothing, the content is empowering. It’s to the point. It is exceptionally motivational, and takes you on a path to helping yourself (you really feel a strong sense of self-achievement as it is a DIY approach) at a gentle pace. I’ve been using it just a week and I’ve started forming habits which are helping me sleep better; insomnia being something I’ve put up with for a long time as well. I’m outside again. Up early again. To bed and off my phone at a responsible time again. Eating regular meals. Drinking more water. Exercising daily for the first time. Telling myself empowering things, and actually believing it.

I’ve been looking through apps for some time now, trying to find the perfect mental well-being assistant. And I have to tell you, it’s Fabulous.

title: Great App for those suffering with mental health issues
body:
I’ve seen a lot of reviews of this app saying that they don’t like being told what to do, which is understandable - but I feel as though this app isn’t getting the praise it deserves. 
I first found this apps Instagram page which I followed due to their helpful tips that they post that do help (seems to be a theme around a little goes a long way) and their app appeared in a snapchat advert and I was convinced to download. 
This app is great for myself - and I’ve suggested for others to download it too - I’ve been deathly struggling with my mental health issues for years now - worsened with my time in university that I’m still enduring and stress from working and familial issues. Starting with just drinking water every day made me look forward to seeing what else I would be able to achieve as time went on. Now I cultivate my daily routines to fit what I’m doing that day - and I feel much more accomplished, even finding short activities that will make me spare time to do my masters degree work when I’m in the darkest of mental places - I’m 22 next week and I’ve honestly never been so productive and genuinely happy (so much so it’s noticeable to friends and family) - in years - and it’s all thanks to this app and the effort I’ve put into using it consistently. 
I really cannot give this app the praise it deserves - and I understand some of you may feel as though it is expensive 
But think of the one off payment as a gift to yourself - it’s £35 for a year - and a year from now you’ll be much better - and much more organised and happier - and the one payment (equal to a meal out) will be more than worth it.

title: Read
body:
To everyone who is upset about this ap. I will try to make a mini tutorial:

1. To cancel the subscription: you can not cancel the subscription WITHIN the ap. Its not just this ap. Its all apps! Thats just how Apple is. Go to App Store>Account settings>manage subscriptions. 

2. You can do other habits other than ‘drinking water’ if you really want to. On the main page if you scroll down it will show two bars ‘morning routine’ and ‘evening routine’. Click on which you want. You can remove habits and add up to 3 on free accounts. It gives you a whole list and if you tap on each habit it explains it a little bit. I will suggest finishing the water one anyway cause you unlock the tree, but you can add two more anyway to the morning. And hey, evening can have 3 new unique ones. 

Overall opinion. I like the app, but not yet enough to purchase, because the meditations and stuff thats available are kind of simple and doesn't do much, making me wonder what type of content is there when I pay. Almost makes me think ‘is it all going to be this non informative and blunt after I pay?’. Basically I’d suggest giving something that is a bit more informative, that can somewhat (not fully) match your premium meditations, so we can be excited and wanting to try those premium ones. Some other meditation apps already do that. They have like 10% available, but they are slightly more informative than a guy telling you to focus on your breathing and staying silent for 5 minutes. Basically bluntly: these apps provide a good bait within free meditations that you wanna try the premium ones. Your bait just isn't fully there yet. The only good bait is that you can add more than one habit.

title: Don’t do it!
body:
Firstly, if you do decide to try the free trial, familiarise yourself with how to cancel APPLE ID subscriptions first. There is no information on this in the app, nor contact details. This means it took me 48 hours to find out how to cancel meaning I am £55 down to an ineffective app. Oh and customer services and Apple will both refuse to refund even within 24 hours of taking the payment. This to me feels quite a lot like they are operating as a scam, relying on duping people out of their money rather than earning it. 

Secondly, the app itself. Well, it’s very busy, with an overload of things to do and click and read. It doesn’t feel like it structures itself for the user, more a messy menu on things for you to find yourself. 
In the first week I found some “inspirational letters” which I could’ve found on a number of free blogs, and an alarm to remind me to drink water in the mornings. As someone who is poor at habits (hence the interest in this app), there’s not enough to actually get me to drink the water - if it was as simple as an alarm on my phone I would’ve set the alarm myself. 

All in all, I wish I’d never bothered.

Maybe the app is “fabulous”, once you start paying for it and get through the beginning stages, but REALLY.....do I need to be reminded to drink water when I wake up? It gives very obvious advice like “carry a water bottle”. The graphics are a bit of a rip off of the game monument valley.

Pretty rubbish....

title: Interesting - but dodgy
body:
This app appears to have a really sound common-sense goal of persuading people to make small incremental changes and wean us all off the all-or-nothing ‘self improvement’ routines that we binge on and then lapse on over and over again.

That much I like. Everything else, not so much. From its Stalinist insistence that you can be perfected, to its ‘don’t think of it as money, think of it as self improvement’ contract straight from the Trump U playbook of high pressure sales. (The app makes you sign a contract of blind trust in it.) Its dodgy. I’m sure the developers will say something clever about behavioural economics, but for me it is a bit of a deal killer.

Also - in signing for the app you get to ‘join sphere’ an ominous and mysterious something that comes with the aforementioned contract and doesn’t tell you what it is but it is sure it will change your life and the weird stilted language doesn’t help. “We’d love to connect with you on a personal level” “you are a special person in our hearts.”  I just keep thinking ‘Fyre Festival’ 

More than that - as noted by the reviewer with chronic fatigue being commanded to sprint every day -although it’s well intended the app’s instance that you exercise no matter if you are sick, that you use your ‘iron core of self discipline’ to ignore your own body’s distress signals, that you are a flawed glob that needs to be perfected, seems to have the potential to do great harm and make users seriously physically and mentally unwell.

I was intrigued by this app because I wanted something that could help me meet my goals, and an app that encourages starting small sounded positive, however the more I use it the more alarm bells it sounds. No one likes to be bullied or gaslit by their own apps, and this app has the feeling of a friend who always acts super chummy and constantly tells you you have put on weight. No one likes to be gaslit by their apps and the more I use it, the more I feel uncomfortable with it.

title: So helpful!
body: Out of all the self development apps/planner apps, fabulous really is fabulous. It’s interactive which I love and the graphics are really cool and engaging definitely keeps me motivated to keep going on there. It’s super easy to use and I like how you can have some additional inspiration in the app if you don’t have a workout routine or need to listen to a guided meditation.
author: Tinico1

title: Change the price!
body:
After only a few days I am intrigued as the habit changers are for life which is excellent. However, the developers need to half the price or more! I would be happy to pay £25 a year for this service and like many other reviewers feel it can make a huge change. Would probably get more subscriptions this way! 

Whilst the research, development and design stages have clearly taken some thought, once you have the formula it seems extortionate at £80 or even £40 as ‘half price’.

title: Motivation in an app that I was lacking
body: I’ve had this app a day so my review is in its infancy but still I have to say this app is amazing. It’s not just a tick this box kind of app but it gives you the most helpful tips to help you stick to your goals. It takes your goals and breaks them into small day to day goals that are much easier to achieve so that before you know it, you’re halfway to achieving your big goal. I am thrilled with this and would recommend it to anyone. I can’t wait to complete my goals and achieve what I assumed I couldn’t.

title: Restrictive
body: I’ve been using this app for 10 days now. Unfortunately it dictates what goal you work on (have more energy) to unlock the others, and it makes you do set activities in order (with one done a certain number of times unlocking the next) with no compromise. I have chronic fatigue syndrome so having more energy isn’t likely, and it insists I tick off morning sprinting etc, which I am physically unable to do. It also insists I have breakfast, which I cannot do as I have to avoid food with medication when I wake up. If I don’t say I have done these activities and log on to confirm every day for a week I am unable to progress through each stage of “having more energy” which I need to complete (which seems to take about a month) in order to unlock other goals. I’m essentially logging on to lie about activities I haven’t done in the hope I could eventually move on and see other goals I may be able to work towards. Nonsense.

title: Good app, but too many plugs for Sphere
body:
I’ve been using Fabulous for a little while now and, whilst I think it’s good in lots of ways, and I understand the developers have a new App to promote, I’m getting a bit fed up with the ‘hard sell’ of Fabulous Sphere. 
I’m sure it’s a great development, and if you had an option to pay monthly I might even be tempted, but nearly £44 is WAY too much in one go for any app, especially when that’s the price with a 50% early sign-up discount! The developers are pricing themselves completely out of the market. Charging less would probably result in more sales, in my opinion. 
It’s a shame, really, as I’m finding Fabulous itself really helpful.
author: HeeBeeFeeBees

title: A simple yet great way to remind yourself that you are amazing!
body:
Yes, my title sounds a little dramatic but this app is so simplistic in it’s approach yet reminds you to take small steps and implement subtle changes in order to just be human, relax and realise your potential.
It begins by setting small challenges, for example, drinking a large glass of water on waking, for three days consecutively. Moving forward it sends you ‘letters’ in order to keep you motivated and open to mind to the humanistic aspect of your existence. It’s all too easy to become focused on your job, family, material possessions that we forget who we really are and the basic needs of being human. This app merely reminds us of the nourishment our brains, bodies and mind needs on a daily basis without being too intrusive. Plus it’s great fun too!

title: Aaargh
body:
App is basic and confusing

I asked for a free one week trial and can find no way of cancelling it before they charge me almost £50 for something that’s telling me to drink some water and get some exercise!

Really, really cheesed off that there’s no easy way to cancel the charge before it hits, and have been sent all round the Apple houses yo try and sort this out!

I’d never have known that it was going to charge me if Apple hadn’t sent a receipt.

The worst kind of in-app purchase is one you do inadvertently, and the developers would do well to reconsider the wisdom of such shark like practise on an app purporting to be about well being!

title: If you've read the books, you'll know how good this is
body:
Based on many things I've read about successful habits and routines, this app is a beautifully made tool which helps to transfer both scientific and anecdotal conclusions into one easy-to-use companion.

I used to have my routines written on my walls - now they are on this app.

An every day user.

Feedback wise, I would say that the explanation of what the subscription service 'Sphere' is is very poor. The box stays on the home feed and can't be removed, yet I've read through it all and it promises a lot without explaining how it would work. It is also very long and provides multiple opportunities to pay for the service (which feels over-suggestive/in your face) and even between these encouragements there's no real development of how Sphere works. With a better, clearer, and more concise (even a quick video) explanation, I'm sure more people would subscribe. Hopefully that's useful to you and can be worked on!
